---
doc_id: D11
title: Orient Steel Ltd. v. Deccan Fabricators
court: SC
year: 2019
bench_size: 2
aliases: (2019) 11 SCC 250
---
[None] IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA (FICTIONAL DEMO). Civil Appeal No. 3030 of 2018.
[Facts] The buyer of steel coils paid an advance of thirty per cent and defaulted; the seller retained the advance.
[Issue] Whether the seller can retain the advance paid under a contract of sale on default by the buyer.
[Reasoning] With great respect, we find it difficult to agree with the breadth of the observations in Ganga Ram v. Union Traders, (1970) 2 SCC 101, in commercial contracts between equals, and we would have been inclined to overrule it. However, being a bench of two judges we are bound by the Constitution Bench decision, and the matter must await a larger bench. Bound by Ganga Ram, we hold the seller may retain only reasonable compensation.
[Decision] The appeal is disposed of with a direction to refund seventy per cent of the advance.
